## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c72ef4040e14592720e8a46cb708ee7d593a6ce7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md + none (the diff is this one file; read, not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` and `packages/spec/src/stack.test.ts` on `origin/main` `f068cde84d` and at each cited merge commit, `examples/app-multi-package/objectstack.config.ts`)

Inputs read: card #33135 body and all four comments (triage 6859219233, seat scope note 6884985712, claim 6885232502, os-dev-report 6885394481); PR #33502 body, file list (one file, +40 / -4) and net diff; the check-runs on this head. Base drift: `git diff b392ff7bdf4 origin/main` is empty for `stack.zod.ts`, `stack.test.ts`, `examples/app-multi-package/` and this ADR, so the PR's base reading holds on today's `main`.

Check-runs on this head at render time: 53 completed, 27 success and 26 skipped. None failed and none is pending. The last to finish were Test Core (1/8) and the three Type Check runs (workspace, consumer gates, debt ledger), all success. The derived gate families answer green.

### ① Derived judgments

- No accept-set change and no public-surface change: the diff is ADR prose only. No schema, export, error code or gate moves. Right.
- The record names two existing refusals, `STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION` and `STACK_NAMESPACE_PREFIX_INVALID`. Both are declared on `main` (`stack.zod.ts`, the `readonly code` lines of `StackSingleAppViolationError` and `StackNamespacePrefixInvalidError`) and raised where the ADR says: `validateSingleApp` and `validateNamespacePrefix` in strict `defineStack`, and `collectComposedSingleAppErrors` in `composeStacks` step 3c. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `skip-changeset` label, no changeset. `docs/adr/**` ships in no package. Right.
- Clause-②: no. Correct. Nothing narrows or widens at the consumer. The ADR records narrowings that already shipped under their own changesets (#32898, #33074 and #33122 each carry `feat(spec)!`).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- Deviation 1 (tier): the dev ran at the claim's default tier and left the contract review to the seat. This record is that review.
- Deviation 2 (signature as a prose line, not an HTML comment): the PR body does carry the prose line. It also ends with a trailing signed HTML comment in the seat's session, which the seat's relay appears to have added. Process only; the contract is unaffected.
- Deviation 3 (the 2026-11-12 paragraph is edited, not kept verbatim): accepted. See nit N4.
- Merge commits named in the diff, each checked against `git log origin/main` after deepening the shallow clone:
  - `0b23b2a0c4` is #32898, merged 2026-11-13.
  - `2c98485db5` is #33074, merged 2026-11-13.
  - `5b2ec820c8` is #33122, merged 2026-11-13.
  - `9ae829108c` (already in the file) is the #32586 merge, PR #32792.

  `git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 0 for all four. The merge dates and SHAs in the Status line and in the new note match `gh api` `merged_at` and `merge_commit_sha`.
- No decision changes. The diff touches only (a) the Status line's "Landed in spec" clause, which gains landings, and (b) D3's dated enforcement notes. D1, D2, D4, the D3 amendment, its reasons, the vocabulary table, "Enforced today, and not yet." and "Not decided here." are byte-identical to `main`.

### ④ Design judgment

`docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md`: the change holds against `main` in substance. Both halves of the old sentence are now false on `main`, and the new note describes the flat-compose refusal, the per-body walk and the namespace-prefix rule correctly as they stand. The per-merge attribution is wrong in one place, and the closing "still not judged" sentence is too broad. Sentence by sentence against the cited code:

- Flat compose, held. `collectComposedSingleAppErrors` sends a result with no `packages[]` to `flatSingleAppFinding`, gated on `SINGLE_APP_PACKAGE_TYPES` (`app`, `module`). The finding refuses two or more composed apps and names each app with `from` and the input label. `SINGLE_APP_COMPOSE_REMEDY` names `manifest: 'preserve'`. `examples/app-multi-package/objectstack.config.ts` composes with `{ manifest: 'preserve' }`. `composeStacks` returns early on `stacks.length === 1`.
- Per-body walk, held. `collectPackageBodySingleAppErrors` judges each body by its own `type`, label and `apps`. `validateSingleApp` returns it next to the top-level finding. With `packages[]`, the top level goes through `residualSingleAppFinding`, the same judge `composeStacks` uses. The residual is read by name through `isResidualTopLevelItem`. "Two or more there are refused" agrees with the code: zero residual hands the case to the body rule.
- Namespace prefix, held. `namespacePrefixErrors` judges each body against `body.namespace` and residual top-level objects against `manifest.namespace`. A body with no namespace returns nothing from `judge`. `defineStack` raises `StackNamespacePrefixInvalidError`.
- `stack.test.ts` pins each of the three, held. The describe holding "refuses a flat composition (the default manifest: 'last') ...", the describe "a packages[] stack is judged per body, and its top level by the residual rule ...", and the describe "a packages[] stack's namespace prefixes are judged per body ...".

Findings:

- **S1 (should-fix): per-body judging at `defineStack` is credited to the wrong merge.** The #33074 bullet says "strict `defineStack` judges a stack that carries `packages[]` per body, each by its own `type`, `id` and `apps`, and its top level by the residual rule". The #32898 bullet says only "Every `packages[]` body of a composition is held to one app too". On the tree of `0b23b2a0c4` (#32898), `validateSingleApp` already ends with `...collectPackageBodySingleAppErrors(config)`, so strict `defineStack` judged every hand-built body from #32898 on. The pin "refuses, at defineStack, a packages[] body that defines two apps" is in `stack.test.ts` at `0b23b2a0c4` and absent at its first parent. #33074's own PR body says "every body is still judged by `collectPackageBodySingleAppErrors` as before". #33074 changed only how the top level of a `packages[]` stack is counted. It refuses an undeclared top-level app beside the manifest-id body's app, and it accepts an additive artifact's repeated top-level apps that #32898's reading refused. So the hand-built-body half of the 2026-11-12 sentence became false at #32898, not at #33074. The card's premise ("since #33074") carried the same error, and the dev's attribution check tested only the residual call. The date "since 2026-11-13" and the Status line, which credits #32898 and #33074 jointly, stay right. Fix:
  - In the #32898 bullet, say every `packages[]` body is held to one app at `composeStacks` and at strict `defineStack` (`#collectPackageBodySingleAppErrors`).
  - In the #33074 bullet, say it changed how strict `defineStack` counts the top level of a `packages[]` stack: by the residual rule instead of every top-level app, with the bodies judged as before.
- **S2 (should-fix): the closing "still not judged" sentence is too broad in two ways.** The sentence reads: "At `defineStack`, package types other than `app` and `module`, a stack with no manifest and `strict: false` are still not judged; a `strict: false` stack that reaches `composeStacks` is judged there."
  - (a) `manifest` and `packages` are each optional in `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`, and no refinement requires a manifest beside `packages[]`. A hand-built stack with no manifest that carries `packages[]` still has every body judged, by `collectPackageBodySingleAppErrors` (single-app) and by `namespacePrefixErrors` (each body against its own namespace). Only its top level goes unjudged. As written, the sentence repeats for that shape the kind of false "not judged" claim this card exists to remove.
  - (b) The sentence comes right after the namespace-prefix bullet, but `composeStacks` runs no namespace-prefix check; nothing in `composeStacks` calls `validateNamespacePrefix` or `namespacePrefixErrors`. It judges a `strict: false` input only by the single-app rule, and only with two or more inputs (the one-input early return).
  - Fix: say a stack with no manifest leaves only its top level unjudged, and say the `composeStacks` judgment of a `strict: false` stack is the single-app rule, with two or more inputs.
- **N1 (nit): the flat-composition description doesn't cover a nested-artifact input.** "Keeps one manifest and puts every input's apps under its id" does not hold when one input carries `packages[]`. The flat result then carries `packages[]` and is judged by the residual rule, and the bodies' flattened copies are accepted. That case is pinned by "accepts a flat composition of a nested artifact whose flattened copy repeats its bodies' apps". The refusal stated in the ADR is still right for inputs with no `packages[]`. A qualifier would do.
- **N2 (nit): path-less symbol anchors.** In the #33074 and #33122 bullets, `#validateSingleApp`, `#residualSingleAppFinding` and `#namespacePrefixErrors` stand with no path in the bullet. Elsewhere in this file, a `#sym` continuation follows a `path#sym` on the same line (reason 1, reason 2). `check:adr-symbol-anchors` does not judge this spelling, as the PR body says. All seven symbols are declared in `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` on `main`, so nothing dangles. Repeating the path once per bullet would make each bullet resolvable on its own.
- **N3 (nit): "the reading at #32586's merge" names an issue.** The merged change is PR #32792 (`9ae829108c`). The file already says "#32586 ... merged as `9ae829108c`", so this follows existing usage. Accepted.
- **N4 (nit, accepted deviation): the 2026-11-12 note is edited rather than kept as written.** The 2026-11-12 note keeps the paragraph before it "as written" and adds a dated note; the new note follows that pattern in heading and form. The one edit to the 2026-11-12 paragraph is a past-tense rewrite of the sentence the card and the seat's scope note (6884985712) asked to drop or rewrite, plus a forward pointer. The new note correctly does not claim the paragraph above is "kept as written". It keeps the reading at that date and changes no decision. Accepted as ruled on the card.

No must-fix. S1 and S2 earn a delta review of their fix. Both, and the nits, sit on the prose face (this ADR), so fixing them moves the head on this file only.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `691fe886ade692706c7dcfb4169918260eea4bc9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md + none (the diff is this one file; read, not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` and `packages/spec/src/stack.test.ts` on `origin/main` `e40cd1e28d` and at each cited merge commit and its parent, `examples/app-multi-package/objectstack.config.ts`)

Inputs read: the earlier record (PR #33502 comment 6885553305, PASS on `c72ef4040e`, S1 and S2 should-fix, N1 to N4 nits); card #33135 body and all four comments (triage 6859219233, seat scope note 6884985712, claim 6885232502, os-dev-report 6885394481); PR #33502 body and file list (one file, +50 / -4 net); the fix delta `git diff c72ef4040e 691fe886ad` (one hunk, inside the 2026-11-13 note only); the check-runs on this head. Base drift: `git diff b392ff7bdf4 origin/main` is empty for `stack.zod.ts`, `stack.test.ts`, `examples/app-multi-package/` and this ADR, so the readings below hold on today's `main`.

Check-runs on this head at render time: 48 completed, 26 success and 22 skipped. None failed and none is pending. Test Core (1/8), Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · repo & tooling gates and Lint · docs & code guards finished last, all success. The derived gate families answer green.

### Delta

- **S1 (should-fix): fixed.** The #32898 bullet now says the same merge holds every `packages[]` body to one app, each by its own `type`, `id` and `apps`, "at `composeStacks` and at strict `defineStack`". On `0b23b2a0c4`, `validateSingleApp` ends with `...collectPackageBodySingleAppErrors(config)` and `collectComposedSingleAppErrors` calls the same walk. At its parent `64c426ab22`, `validateSingleApp` returns early for a non-single-app type and walks no body, and `collectPackageBodySingleAppErrors` is not declared. The pin "refuses, at defineStack, a packages[] body that defines two apps" is in `stack.test.ts` at `0b23b2a0c4`. The #33074 bullet now says it "changes only how strict `defineStack` counts the top level of a stack that carries `packages[]`; the bodies are judged as before. Until then every top-level app counted against `manifest.id`". The `2c98485db5` diff bears this out line by line. At its parent, `own = singleAppFinding(type, label, config.apps)`, which counts every top-level app. At the merge, a `packages[]` stack goes through `residualSingleAppFinding`, and the `collectPackageBodySingleAppErrors` tail is unchanged. The `composeStacks` side of that diff is a refactor that adds the `door` parameter and leaves the head and remedy strings as before, so "changes only" holds.
- **S2 (should-fix): fixed, both halves.**
  - (a) "A stack with no manifest goes unjudged only at its top level: every `packages[]` body it carries is still judged by both rules." On `main`, with no manifest, `validateSingleApp` gets an undefined `type`, so its own finding is undefined, and it still returns `collectPackageBodySingleAppErrors(config)`. `namespacePrefixErrors` still judges each body against `namespaceOf(body)`, and the residual top level against an undefined namespace, which `judge` skips. Right.
  - (b) "`composeStacks` runs no namespace-prefix check" and "A `strict: false` stack meets a rule only when it is one of two or more inputs to `composeStacks`, and then only the single-app rule." On `main` and at `5b2ec820c8`, `validateNamespacePrefix` has one call site, strict `buildDefinedStack`. `namespacePrefixErrors` is called only from `validateNamespacePrefix`. `composeStacks` returns at `stacks.length === 1`, before `collectComposedSingleAppErrors`. A non-strict `defineStack` returns before both `validateNamespacePrefix` and `validateSingleApp`, so "`strict: false` skips both rules" is right too. "Package types other than `app` and `module` are not judged by the single-app rule" is now scoped to that rule, which matches `SINGLE_APP_PACKAGE_TYPES`; the namespace rule judges every type. Right. See N5 for one word.
- **N1 (nit): fixed.** The flat description is now scoped "of inputs that carry no `packages[]`". A new sentence says a result that carries `packages[]` ("under `'preserve'`, or a flat option with an input that carries `packages[]`") is judged by the residual rule instead. In `composeBuiltStacks`, step 3 concatenates an input's `packages`, and step 3a sets `composed.packages` under `'preserve'` when any input has a manifest. `collectComposedSingleAppErrors` then branches on `Array.isArray(composed.packages)`. The pin "accepts a flat composition of a nested artifact whose flattened copy repeats its bodies' apps" is at `0b23b2a0c4`. The residual judge, with name-based `isResidualTopLevelItem`, is there too, so crediting the residual rule for compositions to #32898 is right.
- **N2 (nit): fixed.** Each bullet now carries a full `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts#...` anchor: `#collectComposedSingleAppErrors`, `#residualSingleAppFinding` and `#collectPackageBodySingleAppErrors` in #32898, `#validateSingleApp` in #33074, and `#namespacePrefixErrors` in #33122. `#flatSingleAppFinding` and `#SINGLE_APP_COMPOSE_REMEDY` stay as continuations after a path on the same bullet, as this file does elsewhere. All seven are declared in `stack.zod.ts` on `main`.
- **N3 (nit, accepted): no action owed.** "#32586's merge" is unchanged and follows the file's own usage.
- **N4 (nit, accepted deviation): no action owed.** The 2026-11-12 paragraph is untouched by the delta.

### ① Derived judgments

- No accept-set change and no public-surface change. The delta is ADR prose inside the 2026-11-13 note. No schema, export, error code or gate moves. Right.
- Both refusals the note names, `STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION` and `STACK_NAMESPACE_PREFIX_INVALID`, are raised where it says, as the earlier record found. The delta adds no new code claim beyond those checked under Delta.

### ② Semver level

- `skip-changeset`, no changeset. `docs/adr/**` ships in no package. Right.
- Clause-②: no. Correct. The ADR records narrowings that shipped under their own `feat(spec)!` changesets (#32898, #33074, #33122).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. No new deviation arises from the fix round.
- The merge commits are unchanged from the earlier record. `0b23b2a0c4` (#32898), `2c98485db5` (#33074) and `5b2ec820c8` (#33122) are each squash merges with one parent, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` with `origin/main` exits 0 for each.
- No decision text changed. Against `main`, the PR still touches only the Status line's "Landed in spec" clause (unchanged in this delta), the one past-tense sentence of the 2026-11-12 note (unchanged in this delta) and the new 2026-11-13 note. D1, D2, D4, the D3 amendment and its reasons, the vocabulary table, "Enforced today, and not yet." and "Not decided here." are byte-identical to `main`.

### ④ Design judgment

`docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md`: the fix holds against `main` and against each cited merge. Each new sentence was read against the code. The attribution per merge is now right in all three bullets. The residual description sits where it shipped, at #32898 for `composeStacks`, and #33074 is narrowed to the `defineStack` top-level count it changed. The closing sentence no longer claims anything is unjudged that the code judges. It names the manifest-less stack's bodies, `strict: false` skipping both rules, the single-app scope of the type gate, the two-input condition and the absence of a namespace check in `composeStacks`. The text is wrapped within the file's width.

New findings:

- **N5 (nit): "meets a rule only when" reads wider than the paragraph it closes.** Inside the paragraph's frame, the two spec producers `defineStack` and `composeStacks`, it is exact. But "only" is unscoped. The namespace predicate the note cites, `validateObjectNamespacePrefix`, also runs at the metadata save door (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts`), and `os lint` warns `naming/namespace-prefix` on a loaded config. "Of these two producers" or "in the spec" would close it. No effect on the contract or on any refusal the note records.
- **N6 (nit): the residual sentence in the #32898 bullet does not repeat the type gate.** "A composition whose result carries `packages[]` ... is judged by the residual rule instead" follows a sentence gated on an `app` or `module` manifest. `collectComposedSingleAppErrors` gates the residual judge on the same `SINGLE_APP_PACKAGE_TYPES` check, and "instead" carries that gate. A reader who skims the sentence alone could miss it. Optional.

No must-fix and no should-fix. S1 and S2 are fixed, N1 and N2 are fixed, and N3 and N4 stand as accepted. N5 and N6 are nits and end the round.

## Correction: contract-review tier

The contract-review record(s) 6885553305, 6885829992 on this PR say `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and the seat adopted them as "isolated sub-agent at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER". **That is wrong.** The seat launched the reviewing sub-agent without the tier, so it ran at the seat's own default tier, not at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The seat found this on its own audit. The review was still isolated and adversarial, and its findings stand as an off-tier review. They are not the at-tier record AGENTS.md and the in-seat review ruling require.

The seat re-runs the review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this PR's head and posts that record here. Until it does, this PR has no at-tier record.
